So the WooCommerce ordering query IS honored server-side EVEN THOUGH no <select name='orderby'> and no form.woocommerce-ordering exist in the HTML (both confirmed absent). orderby=date == default (default catalog order already equals date-desc / newest-first), which is the desired watermark order. However this is sort-INDEPENDENT for runtime: doubletap watermark = api-date-since-watermark (WP REST modified_after + orderby=modified), which never uses the HTML sortParam. sortParam=?orderby=date is recorded as verified/honored and matches default order; it is the correct fallback if a future HTML-walk path is ever used.

corrections.round1Hypothesis: R1 candidate set template='/page/{N}' (leading slash, correct). DB carries 'page/{N}/' (no leading slash, broken). Theme B.
corrections.liveMethod: Code trace of buildPaginatedUrl (catalog-crawler.ts:122-125) + trace of which runtime path consumes paginationPattern for this WC site.
corrections.evidence: buildPaginatedUrl type:'path' strips base trailing slash then appends template raw, so template MUST start with '/'. DB 'page/{N}/' on base /product-category/parts/ => /product-category/partspage/2/ (mangled, would 404). R1 '/page/{N}' is correct. BUT: this template is INERT at runtime for doubletap -- see codeFindings theme-B: both the watermark (api-date-since-watermark) and catalog (WC adapter fetchCatalogPage API path) bypass buildPaginatedUrl entirely; it only fires on full-catalog-sweep / html-stream which doubletap does not use.

codeFindings.detail: buildPaginatedUrl type:'path' does `stripped = base without trailing slash; return stripped + template.replace('{N}',n)`. With DB template 'page/{N}/' (no leading slash) and base /product-category/parts/, output = /product-category/partspage/2/ (404). R1 candidate '/page/{N}' (leading slash) is correct. HOWEVER the bug is INERT for doubletapsports at runtime: (1) buildPaginatedUrl is only called in catalog-crawler.ts:781/957/996 (the HTML 'html'-type stream branch, stream.type==='html') and watermark-crawler.ts:649 (full-catalog-sweep Method C ONLY). (2) doubletap's WC adapter has fetchCatalogPage -> catalog-crawler crawlCatalogTier (260-337) takes the API path (paginates via API `page` param, NOT paginationPattern) and only falls to HTML when apiCrawlUsed=false. (3) doubletap's watermark method is api-date-since-watermark (watermark-crawler.ts:746, Method A) which uses adapter.fetchCatalogPage + WP REST modified_after, NOT buildPaginatedUrl. So the broken template never executes for this site. RECOMMENDATION: still fix the template to '/page/{N}' (defensive correctness for any future HTML-fallback), and the runtime defensive-normalization + existing-profile validator proposed in R1 ledger theme-B remain worthwhile fleet-wide, but doubletap is NOT a live coverage blocker from this bug.

WC adapter fetchCatalogPage paginates via API `page`/`per_page` (Store API + WP REST core), independent of profile paginationPattern. getNextPageUrl (248) reads WooCommerce HTML .next.page-numbers links; getNewArrivalsUrl/getNewArrivalsUrls emit ?orderby=date query pagination on /shop/. None consume the profile path template. Confirms theme-B inertness for WC-API sites.

Cloudflare PASSIVE confirmed live: cf-ray on every response, server=cloudflare, cf-cache-status=DYNAMIC, all probes 200, /.env honeypot 404 (no block/challenge), WC Store API + WP REST 200, no challenge set-cookie. hasWaf should be false (crawler routes only on hasWaf boolean). DB stale hasWaf=true over-throttles perPage (intersurplus quantified this theme-D cost at 7.8x). Crawler code path: catalog-crawler.ts:704/290 sets perPage to hasWaf?20:50 default when profile perPage absent, and watermark/full-sweep add WAF empty-page tolerance + Playwright -- all unnecessary overhead for a passive-CF site.

Store API category= filter is RECURSIVE (firearms parent walk == children union, 0 children-only). This invalidates the B15 'add children because parent only shows tiles' heuristic R1 applied here: for WC Store API category walks, the parent already covers all descendants. Adding leaf children only inflates crawl with redundant pages. The real coverage trap on doubletap is the OPPOSITE: dropping 'brands' (a parent with 122 products unique to it) loses 122 products.
